sentences.text: Shri Pankaj Dubey, learned counsels for the applicant.
Shri Sharad Singh, learned P.L. for the respondent/State.
Heard on the question of admission.
This revision is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 3994/2020, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.

This Criminal Revision has been preferred by the applicant against judgment dated 19.02.2020 passed by 12th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal in Criminal Appeal No. 885/2016, arising out of the order dated 15.10.2016 passed by Special Magistrate, Bhopal in R.T. No. 95/2009 whereby the applicant has been convicted for an offence punishable under Section 7(ii) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and sentenced to undergo S.I. for six month with fine of Rs.1,000/- also with default stipulation.
The learned Appellate Court has also affirmed the same.
Applicant is in jail since 19.02.2020.
Brief facts of the case are that on 26.05.2007, Food Inspector-Arvind Kumar has made an inspection in the shop of petitioner namely Milen Sweets.
After giving his introduction, the Food Inspector asked him for food license.
After inspection, the Food Inspector has purchased 6 packets of "Mirch Sev" and after following the rules prescribed in this regard, he sent the sample for examination.
The samples were found mis-branded, thus, he launched the prosecution against the petitioner and his father who died during trial.
The learned trial Court found guilty the applicant for the aforesaid offences and the findings has been affirmed by the Appellate Court.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the learned Courts 2 CRR-1096-2020 below erred in convicting the applicant.

sentences.text:
whereas one Suresh Gupta who is said to be the witness, has not been examined by the prosecution,
however, he has been examined as defence witness.
He further submits that and there is no independent witnesses in this case who supported to the prosecution story.
The learned Court below has also committed the legal error in understanding the deference between the ward 'packed' and 'pre-packed' which denotes the system of packing.

The Court considered the samples as pack nature in some of the paras of judgment but at conclusion, the Court has considered the samples as pre packed, which shows contradictory approach of the trial Court.
The public analyst has also not not examined by the prosecution and an application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. for the same purpose has been rejected by the trial Court.
The seized product has not been produced before the trial Court, moreover, the Food Inspector has not mentioned the contents which are written in on the alleged level.
The Food Inspector has also refused that the 'Sev' was in packed condition.
The prosecution has also not complied with the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act for issuance of notice.
He further submits that the entire prosecution framed against the applicant is an excessive jurisdiction of the State.
The prosecution also suffers from non-joinder of necessary party as the Om Industries are the original manufacture of 'sev' and involved in the packaging of the same.
The applicant only bought the same from Om Industries and sell it accordingly.
The case of prosecution does not found under the definition of mis-branded.
He also argued that under section 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the maximum penalty for sub-standard food or branding is only fine.
It is also submitted that the provisions of the said Act being beneficial to the accused persons can be applied with respect to earlier cases as well, which are pending in the Court.
He has also produced the copy of order passed by co-ordinate bench of this Court in the case of Pawan Kumar Goswami Vs. State of M.P. passed in 3 CRR-1096-2020 Cr.R 5136/2019 , dated 13/11/2019.

sentences.text: Apart from that the applicant is suffering from cardiac disease and if he does not release on bail, he would suffer adversely.
With the aforesaid he prays for allowing this application.
On the other hand learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the submissions.
Heard both the parties and perused the record.

After hearing rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties as well as facts and circumstances of the case, particularly the revision of year 2020 will take considerable time for its conclusion, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicant and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No. 3994/2020 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.
The custodial sentence awarded to the applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision.

Applicant- Santosh Soni be released from custody subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with one surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
The applicant shall appear and mark his presence before trial Court on 14.05.2020 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates as may be given in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
